---
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nf-core/modules/master/modules/environment-schema.json
channels:
  - conda-forge
  - bioconda
dependencies:
  - conda-forge::biopython=1.84
  - conda-forge::python=3.11

---
name: "nf-core/custom/resolvetaxonomy"
description: "Resolve the taxonomy for a set of sequences: use an explicit taxonomy\
  \ file if one\nis given (warning, not silently ignoring, if the sequences also carry\
  \ embedded\ntaxonomy text); otherwise derive taxonomy from each sequence's own FASTA\
  \ header,\nGTDB-style (`>id taxonomy;string`). Headers are always stripped down\
  \ to a bare id\nin the output sequences, regardless of which taxonomy source was\
  \ used. When\ntaxonomy_required is false, records with neither source are dropped\
  \ from the\nresolved taxonomy (with a warning) instead of failing the run.\n"
keywords:
- "taxonomy"
- "fasta"
- "phylogenetics"
tools:
- biopython:
    description: "Freely available tools for computational molecular biology."
    homepage: "https://biopython.org/"
    documentation: "https://biopython.org/wiki/Documentation"
    tool_dev_url: "https://github.com/biopython/biopython"
    doi: "10.1093/bioinformatics/btp163"
    licence:
    - "Biopython License Agreement"
    identifier: "biotools:biopython"
input:
- - meta:
      type: "map"
      description: "Groovy Map containing sample information. e.g. `[ id:'sample1'\
        \ ]`"
  - taxonomy:
      type: "file"
      description: "Optional tab-separated taxonomy labels (seq_name<TAB>rank1;rank2;...).\n\
        Pass `[]` if not available -- taxonomy is then derived from the\nsequences'\
        \ own FASTA headers instead.\n"
      pattern: "*.{tax,tsv,tax.gz,tsv.gz}"
      ontologies:
      - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3475"
  - sequences:
      type: "file"
      description: "Sequences, aligned or not, in FASTA, Clustal or PHYLIP format."
      pattern: "*.{fa,fasta,fna,aln,phy,fa.gz,fasta.gz,fna.gz,aln.gz,phy.gz}"
      ontologies: []
  - taxonomy_required:
      type: "boolean"
      description: "Whether every record must end up with a resolved taxonomy. When\
        \ true, a\nrecord with neither an explicit-file entry nor embedded header\
        \ text fails\nthe run. When false, such records are silently dropped from\
        \ the resolved\ntaxonomy output instead (a warning is still written).\n"
output:
  taxonomy:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information. e.g. `[ id:'sample1'\
          \ ]`"
    - '*.resolved.tax':
        type: "file"
        description: "The resolved taxonomy, either passed through from the input\
          \ file or\nderived from sequence headers. May have fewer records than the\
          \ input\nsequences when taxonomy_required is false.\n"
        pattern: "*.resolved.tax"
        ontologies:
        - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_3475"
  sequences:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information. e.g. `[ id:'sample1'\
          \ ]`"
    - '*.resolved.${resolvedExtension(sequences)}':
        type: "file"
        description: "The input sequences (same format as the input), headers stripped\
          \ down to a bare id."
        pattern: "*.resolved.*"
        ontologies: []
  warnings:
  - - meta:
        type: "map"
        description: "Groovy Map containing sample information. e.g. `[ id:'sample1'\
          \ ]`"
    - '*.warnings.txt':
        type: "file"
        description: "One line per warning (e.g. embedded taxonomy text ignored, or\
          \ records dropped); empty if none."
        pattern: "*.warnings.txt"
        ontologies:
        - edam: "http://edamontology.org/format_2330"
  versions_biopython:
  - - ${task.process}:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the process"
    - biopython:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the tool"
    - python3 -c 'import Bio; print(Bio.__version__)':
        type: "eval"
        description: "The expression to obtain the version of the tool"
topics:
  versions:
  - - ${task.process}:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the process"
    - biopython:
        type: "string"
        description: "The name of the tool"
    - python3 -c 'import Bio; print(Bio.__version__)':
        type: "eval"
        description: "The expression to obtain the version of the tool"
